what: The protocol says to run eval/eval_test_runner.sh in the foreground, and CLAUDE.md forbids backgrounding device runners, but a whole golden directory for this op takes ~12 min of wall time — longer than the Bash tool max timeout (600 s). My first invocation was killed at 10 min (exit 143): the wrapper died while the underlying pytest kept running and holding the device flock, and /tmp/tt-device.dirty was left set, so the state was ambiguous (had it finished? was the device wedged? was it safe to relaunch?). I only recovered by ps-grepping for the orphan, letting it finish, and then re-running the second pass as nohup-plus-poll. Any op whose golden suite exceeds 10 min hits this identically.
suggest: State the sanctioned long-run pattern in the verifier prompt next to the eval_test_runner.sh command: launch it detached (nohup ... > <results_dir>/runner.log 2>&1 &) and poll golden_results.txt / runner.log with sleep, noting that eval_test_runner.sh holds its own flock and resets the device itself (so it is exempt from the run_safe_pytest.sh no-background rule), and that a tool-timeout kill does NOT stop the inner pytest.

ref: incremental-verifier prompt, Testing Protocol step 2 (verify_supported invocation)
what: The prompt gives the verifier CLI as a bare `python3 -m eval.verify_supported <results_dir> ttnn.operations.{op_name} ...`. Run that way it fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named ttnn.operations.rms_norm — the repo ttnn is only importable from python_env. It is easy to misread the failure as the op module being mis-registered / the package __init__ missing an export (i.e. an op-side defect to go fix) rather than a missing venv, because the adjacent eval_test_runner.sh command needs no activation (it sources the env itself).
suggest: Write the command as `source python_env/bin/activate && python3 -m eval.verify_supported <results_dir> ttnn.operations.{op_name} --output <results_dir>/verifier_report.json`, or add a one-line note that unlike eval_test_runner.sh the CLI needs the venv activated.
